pool.text: Badr al-Gamali loosened restrictions, allowing richer families from Fustat to move into the city.
Saladin began construction on the Cairo Citadel to serve as the government seat.
Power transitioned to the Mamluks during the Seventh Crusade after al-Salih died.
Traveller Ibn Battuta visited and described the city as Egypt's principal district.
The Ottomans conquered Egypt after defeating Sultan al-Ghuri in the battle.
Café Riche opened and became a meeting place for intellectuals and revolutionaries.
The current bridge was completed in an Art Deco style.
The Cairo Fire riots devastated the city with the destruction of downtown shops.
The first Cairo International Film Festival was launched by the Egyptian Association.
Cairo's historic center was awarded World Heritage Site status.
The Cairo Metro opened as the oldest metro system in Africa.
President Mubarak inaugurated the new Cairo Opera House.
Cairo was hit by an earthquake causing 545 deaths and leaving people homeless.
The first environmental acts were introduced in Cairo to improve the situation.
The economy of Cairo was ranked first in the Middle East.
Cairo's Tahrir Square was the focal point of the revolution against Mubarak.
The third line of the Cairo Metro opened after initial planning.
Plans were announced for a new city to be built east of Cairo.
Plans to construct two monorail systems were announced.
The government completed the erection of a new monument featuring an ancient obelisk.
